items.description_html:
RT Surenddra verma
Great Punjabi Lala Jagat Narain.
He spent years in prison for opposing both British rule and the Emergency. He built Punjab Kesari into one of Punjab's most widely read newspapers and refused to bow before terror.

He stood up to Bhindranwale despite repeated threats. He was assassinated for his courage. The sacrifices did not end there-his son, Ramesh Chander, was also killed, along with 52 members of the Punjab Kesari family.

The media group lost:
• 2 Editors
• 7 Reporters
• 20 Distribution Agents
• 23 Hawkers
• 2 Workers

Their only "crime" was refusing to surrender to Khalistani intimidation and continuing to print the truth.

Punjab Kesari also raised funds and supported the families of Hindu and Sikh civilians murdered by Khalistani terrorists when the state had largely failed them.

When fear forced distributors to stop carrying the newspaper, KPS Gill ensured copies were distributed through police stations so the voice of truth would not be silenced.

Lala Jagat Narain, the Punjab Kesari family, and KPS Gill remind us that Punjab was saved not only by brave security personnel but also by fearless journalists and ordinary citizens who refused to bow before terror.

Their sacrifice must never be forgotten. 🇮🇳

items.title: RT Reads with Ravi: Umberto Eco, who owned 50,000 books, had this to say about home libraries: “It is foolish to think that you have to read all the ...
items.description_html:
RT Reads with Ravi
Umberto Eco, who owned 50,000 books, had this to say about home libraries:

“It is foolish to think that you have to read all the books you buy, as it is foolish to criticize those who buy more books than they will ever be able to read. It would be like saying that you should use all the cutlery or glasses or screwdrivers or drill bits you bought before buying new ones.

“There are things in life that we need to always have plenty of supplies, even if we will only use a small portion.

“If, for example, we consider books as medicine, we understand that it is good to have many at home rather than a few: when you want to feel better, then you go to the ‘medicine closet’ and choose a book. Not a random one, but the right book for that moment. That’s why you should always have a nutrition choice!

“Those who buy only one book, read only that one and then get rid of it. They simply apply the consumer mentality to books, that is, they consider them a consumer product, a good. Those who love books know that a book is anything but a commodity.”

items.title: RT Sann: His name is Dinesh Thakur. He gave up a safe, high paying job and spent eight years of his life fighting one of the largest drug companies in...
items.description_html:
RT Sann
His name is Dinesh Thakur.

He gave up a safe, high paying job and spent eight years of his life fighting one of the largest drug companies in the country. He did it because he discovered that the medicines millions of people trusted were built on a lie.

He was a chemical engineer who had worked in America and come back to India for a senior role at Ranbaxy, then the biggest generic medicine maker in the country. It was a proud Indian company whose cheap medicines were sold across the world.

Not long after he joined, he was asked to look into the quality of the company's drugs. What he found frightened him.

The company was faking its test results. Medicines were being sold without being properly tested for whether they were safe, or whether they even worked. The data handed to regulators was simply invented.

These were not luxury goods. These were the tablets that sick people swallowed every day, trusting that they would heal them.

Thakur went to his own bosses with what he had found. Nothing changed. So he made a choice that cost him everything. He resigned, and he reported the company to the American drug regulators.

Then began eight long years. He handed over evidence, sat through investigation after investigation, and lived under the shadow of taking on a giant that had every reason to crush him.

In 2013, it ended. Ranbaxy admitted its guilt in an American court, pleaded guilty to seven serious crimes, and was made to pay one of the largest fines ever handed to a generic drug maker, five hundred million dollars.

Because one man refused to look away, the way the world checks the safety of its medicines was changed for good.

He had a comfortable life and a good salary. He gave it all up so that the medicine in a stranger's hand could be trusted.

items.title: RT The Seeker: It's a shame no major film has been made about Biju Patnaik. He lived a life that sounds almost fictional: In 1938, he flew his entire ...
items.description_html:
RT The Seeker
It's a shame no major film has been made about Biju Patnaik. He lived a life that sounds almost fictional:

In 1938, he flew his entire wedding procession by aircraft to Rawalpindi for his marriage to Gyanwati Sethi (who became the first Indian woman to hold a commercial pilot’s license, and the couple later flew daring missions together.)

While serving in the Royal Indian Air Force (including as head of Air Transport Command), he secretly ferried freedom fighters like Jayaprakash Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia, and Aruna Asaf Ali to their hideouts. He also airdropped 'Quit India' leaflets to Indian troops while evacuating British families.

The British once jailed him for transporting nationalist leaders and distributing anti-British literature but also honored him for bravery in evacuating civilians from Japanese-occupied Burma.

During WWII, he flew daring missions delivering arms and supplies to Soviet forces in Stalingrad, and over the treacherous 'Hump' route to China in
support of Chinese Nationalist forces against the Japanese.

In July 1947, he and his wife flew a Dakota into Indonesia, landed on an improvised airstrip while evading Dutch anti-aircraft fire, rescued Prime Minister Sutan Sjahrir, refuelled using abandoned Japanese fuel, and flew him safely to India via Singapore.

A couple of months later, during the Pakistani invasion of Kashmir, he airlifted one of the first Indian troops into Srinagar.

The same year he founded Kalinga Airlines, one of India's earliest private airlines.

As Odisha CM post-1962 India-China war, he secretly visited CIA headquarters at Langley to forge a covert India-US partnership against China, which led to the Aviation Research Centre (ARC) at Charbatia, which supported U-2 recon missions over Tibet.

He was also a legendary administrator and statesman, laying much of the foundation of Odisha's industrial empire (mines, ports, heavy industries etc).

When he passed away, Indonesia observed 7 days of state mourning. Russia observed 1 day. He remains the only person in Indian history whose body was draped in the national flags of 3 nations - India, Indonesia, and Russia.

Few public figures have left such a footprint.

His extraordinary life needs to be brought to the big screen.


Shiv Aroor: What event in Indian history/recent current affairs do you want to see a film made on?

Our monthly newsletter is out from @icfi_indicus with the latest news and views curated on #financialinclusion

"Over the past year, one message has come through clearly - as extreme weather events grow more frequent and severe, it cannot be business as usual anymore. Central banks across the globe have accepted climate risk as a core banking risk, and some of the world’s largest pension and investment firms are incorporating climate black-swan risks in their decision making. For India, there is an additional imperative: climate resilience must be placed at the heart of our financial inclusion agenda. It is not just a policy obligation - financial service providers must look beyond mere compliance. We need credit and insurance products that protect the most vulnerable households and businesses from the growing financial costs of weather shocks."

items.description_html:
Not one partner. Not a handful. One in five.

A Fifth of Nvidia's China Partners Have Sold Into the Blacklist.

India Angle

The centre of gravity in chip policy is shifting from the licensable unit to the reseller, and that reframes India from a passive importer into a jurisdiction whose channel gets audited. Value added resellers and system integrators are the layer under scrutiny here, and India has the same layer standing between global vendors and domestic buyers.

The falsifiable test is whether Indian integrators begin facing formal end user certification, resale restrictions and beneficial ownership disclosure on accelerator sales within the next two procurement cycles.

Volume held flat while documentation load rises would confirm it.

items.description_html:
India Built a Phone Export Industry. Now It Needs Customers It Doesn't Have.

India's handset export scheme is aimed at a global market where roughly 61% of units sit outside Apple and Samsung and are served by Chinese brands using Chinese assemblers. The binding constraint is therefore anchor customer access, not incentive quantum or installed capacity, which is why the same policy tool that worked domestically may not repeat offshore.

This is falsified if a non Apple Indian assembler announces a multi year export contract with a top ten global brand.

items.description_html:
.@federalreserve holds interest rates steady for 5th meeting in a row, but three voting members are ready to hike. 10-year Treasury yield jumps 7 bps & 30-year bond yield hits its highest level since 2007 after fixed-income investors digest the hawkish tone on inflation from the central bank.
•Members are ready for a hike: In the first split vote of the Warsh era, three FOMC members would prefer to raise rates in the face of elevated inflation.
•Warsh is trademarking his communication style: The new chair is opposed to forward guidance, preferring that markets and businesses react to real-time financial information.
•FOMC is letting markets take the lead: Warsh wants markets to react to economic shocks and news events in real time, rather than relying on Fed projections.

items.title: Where's FCNR(B) flow gone? @kantisoumya of @TheOfficialSBI says, they are in transit. So far (8 June-17 Jul), FCA up by $7.6 bn, while RBI deposit mob...
items.description_html:
Where's FCNR(B) flow gone? @kantisoumya of @TheOfficialSBI says, they are in transit.
So far (8 June-17 Jul), FCA up by $7.6 bn, while RBI deposit mobilization was $17.4 bn for FCNR(B) flows.
While RBI provides weekly change in FCA every Friday, every bank has a designated time during the week to swap these FCNR(B) deposits with RBI and get equivalent rupee resources. It's possible that FCNR(B) deposit numbers are being captured by RBI and becomes a part of FCA with a lag --with assumption that a large part of foreign exchange reserves is being recouped & adding to RBI's foreign exchange coffers.

Owing to this,  we expect for the next 15 days period (17 Jul-31 Jul) FCA inflows could touch $10-12 billion based on current trends.

It may also be noted that once the swap is done, there will be a corresponding liquidity injection (permanent and temporary) Thus, bank time deposits/ permanent monetary injection have increased by close to Rs 90,000 crores. Core liquidity / Temporary liquidity injection has already at ~Rs 5 lakh crore as of June 30 clearly indicating the impact of FCNR (B) inflows on liquidity.

items.title: Tear gas, lathi charges, pellets, blocking supply of food & water can't do anything to cockroaches They have been around 300+ million years -- predate...
items.description_html:
Tear gas, lathi charges, pellets, blocking supply of food & water can't do anything to cockroaches
They have been around 300+ million years -- predate dinosaurs by 150 million years.
Cockroaches can live for a week without a head.
They can survive a month without food & 2 weeks without water.
They eat anything -- glue, hair, and book bindings.
They can hold their breath for 40 minutes & survive submerged underwater up to 30 minutes.
They have decentralized nervous system. Each of leg-controlling ganglia can operate independently; that’s why a headless roach can still stand & react.
They're incredibly fast; can sprint roughly 50 body lengths per second (like running 200+ mph by a human being).
They can run on 2 legs. At top speed, some cockroaches sprint bipedally, like tiny dinosaurs & move faster.
They can withstand radiation doses many times higher than what's lethal to humans.
They can flatten their bodies and squeeze through gaps as thin as a coin.
A single female can produce hundreds of offspring in a lifetime & they can reproduce without males.
Cockroaches make group decisions democratically. They "vote" on where to shelter. They use collective behaviour to distribute themselves optimally, balancing between staying together and not overcrowding one place.
They can learn and be trained.
They have "personalities." Some are risk-takers who explore exposed areas quickly; others stay cautious and hidden, and these traits stay stable over time.

items.title: Between June 8 & July 17, India attracted $20.7 billion forex inflow under RBI scheme which will remain operational till Sept 30. It's a puzzle for me...
items.description_html:
Between June 8 & July 17, India attracted $20.7 billion forex inflow under RBI scheme which will remain operational till Sept 30.
It's a puzzle for me: Where's the forex flow gone?
It's neither reflecting on forex reserves nor on INR liquidity (INR to flow, following swaps).
On June 12, forex reserves were $671.6 bn. Out of this, foreign currency $544.3 bn.
On July 17, forex reserves $676.2 bn & foreign currency $551 bn.
Rise of just around $6 bn. What happened to the rest?
Why is forex flow not reflecting on reserves?
1. RBI selling dollars in spot market.
2. It's allowing forward book ( Buy/Sell position)  to mature (not rolling over).
3. Customers withdrawing from existing FCNR(B)/NRE accounts and putting it back through new FCNB scheme.
We see new flows in FCNB but not outflow from the existing pile.
Welcome to throw light ...
(Illustration courtesy @livemint )

items.description_html:
RT Kimberly Clausing
(1/2) My new blog out today with Maurice Obstfeld.

We discuss why so-called "optimal tariffs" are far from optimal.

In part 1 today, we show problems with the textbook argument, and note that other tax instruments are superior for the underlying aims.


Peterson Institute: "Optimal" tariffs are misnamed, @KClausing & Maurice Obstfeld write, & do not lead to a net gain in national welfare in practice—in fact, they harm US interests. Tariffs are also not an efficient way to shift tax burdens from US residents onto foreigners. https://www.piie.com/blogs/realtime-economics/2026/optimal-tariffs-are-far-optimal-part-1

items.description_html:
RT Peterson Institute
NEW: What's the status of US-China decoupling? How have Trump's tariffs in 2018-19 plus 2025 affected supply chains & US imports? @ChadBown explores.
💡Despite the US tariff actions, US real goods imports from the world in 2025 increased by 4% over 2024 levels.
📈By the end of 2025, US imports from the world remained above the pre-Trump 1.0 trade war linear trend.
📉US imports from China fell by 28% in 2025.
📈US imports from the rest of the world increased by 9%.
🇨🇳China’s share of US imports fell from nearly 22% in the 12 months before June 2018 to only 9% in 2025.
Other economies significantly increased their shares of US imports...
🇹🇼Taiwan by 4.1 percentage points
🇻🇳Vietnam by 3.7 points
🇲🇽Mexico by 2.3 points

💡The US imports from China hit hardest in Trump’s second trade war were those that were omitted from his first.
📈At the beginning of 2025, imports of products that had been omitted from tariffs during the first Trump administration were greater than they were before the Trump 1.0 trade war.
🗓️A 20% tariff on those goods by March 2025 led to a sharp decline in China's exports to the US.
📉In contrast, US imports of Chinese goods that had been hit with 25% tariffs in 2018–19 had already dropped by roughly 40% by the January 2025 inauguration.
